sentences.text: 4 2. Heard the arguments of both the sides and perused the records available on record in all these appeals.
3. Brief facts of the case are that the injured/claimants in all these appeals met with an accident on 19.12.2021 and sustained grievous injuries.
Hence, they filed their respective claim petitions before the NC: 2025:KHC-K:6530 HC-KAR Tribunal seeking compensation from the respondents.

The Tribunal after considering the entire evidence on record, awarded the compensation of Rs.4,56,500 in MVC No.844/2022, compensation of Rs.1,35,400/- in MVC No.845/2022 and compensation of Rs.1,77,100/- in MVC No.843/2022, with interest at 6% per annum from the date of petition till realization and held respondent No.1 liable to pay compensation to the claimants and exonerated respondent No.2 - Insurance Company from its liability.
4. Aggrieved by the said award, the appellants- claimants have preferred these appeals.

But at this stage, it is submitted by the learned counsel for the appellants in all these appeals that there is no dispute regarding quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal and they only seek for an order of 'pay and recover' relying on NC: 2025:KHC-K:6530 HC-KAR the judgment of the Apex Court in the case of Pappu Vs. Vinod Kumar Lamba1.
5.

No doubt, the Tribunal has rightly observed that there is no valid Driving License and there is violation of the terms and conditions of the Policy and hence, respondent No.1-owner of the vehicle is liable to pay the compensation to the claimants.

However, in view of ratio laid down in the above citation, this Court finds it reasonable to direct respondent No.2 - Insurance Company to pay the compensation to the claimants at the first instance and thereafter recover the same from respondent No.1.
6.

In the result, the following order is passed:
 (i) Appeals are allowed in part.
(ii) The impugned judgments and awards are modified in respect of liability only and rest of the order remained unaltered.

(2018) 3 SCC 208 NC: 2025:KHC-K:6530 HC-KAR (iii) Respondent No.2 - Insurance Company is directed to deposit the compensation amount awarded by the Tribunal along with interest within one month from the date of this judgment.
(iv) Liberty is given to the Insurance Company to recover the same from respondent No.1 on due process of law.

sd/-
(P. SREE SUDHA) JUDGE SBS CT:RJ Mahantesh @ Mahesh vs Siddappa And Anr on 3 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/156877567/
